{"path":"/study","markdown":"# Verification report: pitzDaily

foam-verify 0.0.1, from `study.toml`: 4 levels, finest first; refined = mesh; grid sequence structured; refined directions d = 2; formal order 2.

## Verdict

**Not a clean pass.** 0 of 1 quantity of interest are clean passes.

| QoI | Finest grid | Relative U | Grid convergence | Clean pass |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `dp` | -3.479218 | n/a | divergence, R = -4.422 | no |

What stops a clean pass:

- `dp`: convergence ratio R = (phi2 - phi1)/(phi3 - phi2) = -4.422: |R| >= 1, oscillatory divergence (Eca and Hoekstra 2014)
- `dp`: the solution is not grid-converged, so no GCI is given
- `dp`: level 139k: drifting: over the last 142 samples (x = 1278 to 1419): relative range 0.319, relative drift -0.332; the drift exceeds tol = 0.001, so the QoI is still changing
- `dp`: level 62k: drifting: over the last 82 samples (x = 730 to 811): relative range 0.185, relative drift 0.179; the drift exceeds tol = 0.001, so the QoI is still changing
- `dp`: level 28k: drifting: over the last 50 samples (x = 391 to 440): relative range 0.169, relative drift 0.131; the drift exceeds tol = 0.001, so the QoI is still changing

## Levels

| Level | Folder | Cells | r to the next coarser |
|---|---|---|---|
| 139k | `n139k` | 139,025 | 1.494 |
| 62k | `n62k` | 62,257 | 1.499 |
| 28k | `n28k` | 27,703 | 1.505 |
| 12k | `n12k` | 12,225 |  |

## Settings consistency

**Pass.** The levels differ only in the mesh.

Compared on every level: `system/fvSchemes`, `system/fvSolution`, `constant/transportProperties`, `constant/turbulenceProperties`, `0/U`, `0/epsilon`, `0/k`, `0/nut`, `0/p`, `system/controlDict`.

## `dp`

**Not a clean pass.** -3.479218, with no uncertainty estimate.

From `postProcessing/pressureDrop/*/multiFieldValue.dat`, column `Group0`, mean over the window; window: the last 10% of the samples, at least 50.

| Check | Result | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| Grid convergence | fail | grids 1-3: convergence ratio R = (phi2 - phi1)/(phi3 - phi2) = -4.422: \|R\| >= 1, oscillatory divergence (Eca and Hoekstra 2014); the solution is not grid-converged, so no GCI is given |
| Refinement ratio | pass | r21 = 1.494, r32 = 1.499; at least 1.3 (Celik et al. 2008, step 2) |
| Observed order | n/a | not defined: divergence, R = -4.422 |
| Asymptotic range | n/a | checked only for monotonic convergence |
| Coarser triplets | fail | grids 2-4: oscillatory, R = -0.5800 |
| Iterative convergence | fail | drifting on every level (tol 0.001) |
| Iterative error | n/a | no discretisation uncertainty U to compare with |
| Settings consistency | pass | the levels differ only in the mesh (10 files compared) |
| Refined directions | pass | dim = 2, with empty or wedge patches on every level: frontAndBack |
| Refinement scope | assumed | scope mesh: assumes every cell, near-wall layers included, was refined by the same ratio (Celik et al. 2008, step 2: systematic refinement, geometrically similar cells) |
| Grid sequence | assumed | grid sequence structured: the levels refine one base grid systematically (the base grid may itself be unstructured), so Fs = 1.25 with three or more grids (ASME V&V 20, para. 2-4.1) |

| Level | Value | Iterative | Window | Relative range | Relative drift | u_it | u_it / U |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 139k | -3.479218 | drifting | 142 of 1419, 1278 to 1419 | 0.32 | -0.33 |  |  |
| 62k | -5.144006 | drifting | 82 of 811, 730 to 811 | 0.18 | 0.18 |  |  |
| 28k | -4.767537 | drifting | 50 of 440, 391 to 440 | 0.17 | 0.13 |  |  |
| 12k | -5.416616 | drifting | 50 of 279, 230 to 279 | 0.12 | -0.11 |  |  |

| Grids | Convergence | Result | Relative U |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1-3 | divergence, R = -4.422 | -3.479218 | n/a |
| 2-4 | oscillatory, R = -0.5800 | -5.144 +/- 0.974 | 19% |

Notes:

- 4 grids: one result per consecutive triplet; the verdict is from grids 1-3.
- coarser triplet (grids 2-4): oscillatory_convergence
- level 12k (not in the headline result): drifting: over the last 50 samples (x = 230 to 279): relative range 0.12, relative drift -0.112; the drift exceeds tol = 0.001, so the QoI is still changing

## Method

- Grid convergence after Celik et al. (2008), with the convergence types of Eça and Hoekstra (2014): Fs = 1.25 on three or more grids of a structured grid sequence, and 3 for an unstructured sequence (ASME V&V 20, para. 2-4.1), on two grids, or when p is outside [0.5, 4]; refinement ratios of at least 1.3; an asymptotic-range ratio within [0.9, 1.1]; with four or more grids, every coarser triplet converges monotonically too. Above the formal order, U uses the formal order (ASME V&V 20, Appendix C-4); the Richardson numbers and the checks keep the observed p. An oscillatory triplet gets a spread bound and never a clean pass (foam-verify docs/gci.md).
- Iterative convergence of each QoI from its own history over the window given with it: converged when its relative range and relative drift are within tol, and u_it is half the range. On the grids behind the result, u_it must be at most U/100 (ASME V&V 20, para. 2-4; docs/iterative.md).
- Settings consistency: the schemes, solver settings, physical properties, boundary conditions and near-wall layer settings of the levels, compared entry by entry (docs/consistency.md).
- U is the uncertainty of the finest-grid value, and the band is that value +/- U. A QoI is a clean pass only when no check fails (docs/report.md).
"}

**No. dp is neither converged nor mesh-independent, so I can't give it an uncertainty.** The finest grid (139k cells) gives dp = −3.479, but there's no valid uncertainty band for that number. Two separate things are wrong:

**1. The grid study diverges.** Here is the value on each level, finest first:

| Level | Cells | dp |
|---|---|---|
| 139k | 139,025 | −3.479 |
| 62k | 62,257 | −5.144 |
| 28k | 27,703 | −4.768 |
| 12k | 12,225 | −5.417 |

- For the three finest grids, the convergence ratio R = (φ₂−φ₁)/(φ₃−φ₂) is −4.42. Because |R| is at least 1, the value is swinging back and forth with growing steps, so there is no observed order, no Richardson extrapolation and no GCI.
- The biggest change is the last one: going from 62k to 139k cells moves dp by about 32%.
- The three coarser grids (62k, 28k, 12k) do oscillate inward (R = −0.58) and give roughly ±19%. That says nothing about the finest-grid value, and an oscillating result never counts as a clean pass anyway.

**2. No level has finished converging iteratively.** dp is still drifting on every grid over its averaging window, which is the last 10% of samples (at least 50). The tolerance is 0.001:

| Level | Relative range | Relative drift |
|---|---|---|
| 139k | 0.32 | −0.33 |
| 62k | 0.18 | 0.18 |
| 28k | 0.17 | 0.13 |
| 12k | 0.12 | −0.11 |

The runs also stopped after different numbers of samples (1419, 811, 440 and 279). They look like they ended before reaching steady state. That probably explains the erratic differences between grids: the iterative error is as large as the differences between grids, so it drowns out any sign of how the mesh affects dp.

The settings check passed: the levels differ only in the mesh, across 10 compared files. The refinement ratios are about 1.5, which meets the 1.3 minimum, so the grid sequence itself is reasonable.

**What to do:** Run each level until dp levels off. Check the residuals too, and consider under-relaxation if the solution really oscillates. Then run the grid study again. Only after that will the finest-grid value carry a meaningful GCI.

FINAL: converged=no; value=-3.479218; uncertainty=none
